text:
Evelyn: Hit a weird failure when rotating an org API key. Our background worker (spawned via child_process.fork) kept hitting 401s; the web server in the same process was fine.

Marco: fork inherits env at spawn time. Are you mutating process.env after fork?

Evelyn: Yes. We read ephemeral session from keyring at runtime and set process.env.REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN = token, then fork. But the worker is started earlier by PM2 and never restarted.

Yuki: PM2 starts processes on boot; if it forks a child, updating parent.env later doesn't update already-running children. Two options: 1) ensure token is available before workers start, 2) pass token down when spawning, or 3) have SDKs expose a provider so each request reads fresh creds.

Marco: Short-term patch I applied: when we refresh token, send an IPC message to children to update their env and recreate client instances. Not ideal but works for our monolith. Example: `child.send({type:'cred:update', token})` then in worker `process.on('message', m => if (m.type==='cred:update') client.reload(m.token))`.

Evelyn: That's helpful. But sampleapps and server templates don't show this pattern. New hires get stuck.

Yuki: For a systemic fix: Node SDK should accept `credentialProvider` (sync or async) and call it per-connection for long-lived connections (streams) or per-request for short calls. That avoids relying on env mutation. Python and Go already have equivalents; Node parity would fix a lot.

Marco: Also find-and-replace needed: we still have `REDWOOD_TOKEN` and `RLW_SESSION` in a few legacy examples. Let's pick canonical names: REDWOOD_API_KEY (long-lived) and REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN (ephemeral). Add a deprecation banner in CLI when it sees old names.

ops-bot: Created ticket DEVX-2103: "credential provider parity (Node) + canonical env names + sampleapp child-proc cookbook" and linked checklist.

Evelyn: Action items: Yuki -> spec Node provider API; Marco -> add child-proc IPC helper in sampleapp; Docs -> add small cookbook (spawn env vs ipc) + recommend `rlw login --export` pattern for shells. I'll file sampleapp PRs after reviews. :white_check_mark:

Marco: One more: for k8s, prefer projected secrets or CSI drivers and a sidecar that updates env via SIGHUP or restarts container gracefully. Add a note to infra runbook.

Yuki: I'll sync provider spec with SDK owners so behavior is consistent across streaming, SSE, and websocket clients.

Evelyn: Thanks all — saved my morning and another oncall pager. :)
